item.title: Patriots’ Mike Vrabel doesn’t sound thrilled about catching up with Tom Brady before he calls Packers game
item.description: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Patriots’ Mike Vrabel doesn’t sound thrilled about catching up with Tom Brady before he calls Packers game appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Tom Brady will return to Gillette Stadium on Sunday, but this time he won’t be wearing a Patriots uniform. The seven-time Super Bowl champion will be at the stadium as a FOX Sports broadcaster for New England ‘s Week 9 matchup against the Green Bay Packers. His return also gives former teammates a chance to reconnect. However, Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel did not sound particularly excited when asked about catching up with Brady. “I think I’m required contractually to catch up with him at some point,” Vrabel joked during Wednesday’s press conference. “I’m sure it’ll be a Zoom. I’m sure they won’t show up here. I’m sure it will be on Zoom.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Vrabel added that he expected to see Brady at Rob Gronkowski’s Patriots Hall of Fame induction on Saturday. Gronkowski, who also works for FOX Sports, will be honored at Gillette Stadium. Vrabel and Brady spent eight seasons together in New England from 2001 to 2008, winning three Super Bowls. Their relationship has remained friendly since their playing days ended. Vrabel previously described Brady as a friend and confirmed that they exchanged texts after Super Bowl LX. Brady has also spoken about returning to the stadium, admitting the occasion will bring back plenty of memories. “It’ll be certainly emotional,” Brady said. He recalled the memorable games and championship moments he experienced at Gillette Stadium and praised the Patriots organization. Sunday will mark Brady’s first appearance at the venue as a FOX Sports broadcaster . He previously returned for his Patriots Hall of Fame induction in 2024 and the unveiling of his statue in 2025. The reunion will bring several familiar faces together again, even if Vrabel’s scheduled conversation with his former quarterback may have to happen over Zoom. item.title: Lakers face fresh Bronny James roster questions after former No. 1 pick’s explosive criticism
item.description: Eric Thayer / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images Kwame Brown has delivered a brutal assessment of Bronny James’ place on the Los Angeles Lakers roster, questioning why the third-year guard continues to occupy an NBA spot. The former No. 1 overall pick believes Bronny has taken an opportunity away from another player who worked hard to reach the league, with LeBron James’ influence central to his criticism. The Lakers have made a strong start to the 2026-27 season, sitting at 6-2 after eight games. However, Bronny has featured in just four of those contests, playing only 11 minutes in total. Kwame Brown questions Bronny James’ place on the Los Angeles Lakers roster Speaking on his YouTube channel, Brown did not hold back when discussing Bronny’s limited contributions and the circumstances surrounding his place in the team. The former Lakers teammate of Kobe Bryant said: “This is the National Basketball Association. This ain’t for the little boys and wimps. This is professional, and what I saw, I just don’t get it. It’s mind-blowing how somebody lost a job to that. Some kid that worked their b*** off, that really feels like they could have made the NBA, they lost their job to that. And the only reason why everybody is okay with it is because of his father. This is a shame, what we’re actually seeing. Call it hate, call it whatever you want. To me it’s a shame.” Brown’s comments followed two difficult appearances for Bronny. Against the Toronto Raptors, he finished with no points, one turnover and a minus-11 rating in roughly two minutes. His next outing against the Miami Heat brought two points from a single made shot, but he played for only around a minute. Brown was equally unimpressed, describing the brief spell against Miami as: “the worst 90 seconds of basketball I ever seen in my life.” The criticism comes as the Lakers look to maximise Luka Doncic’s prime years. The Athletic’s Jovan Buha has suggested the franchise could consider moving on from Bronny or Jaden Hardy to create roster flexibility. Bronny is earning $2.3 million this season and has a team option for 2027-28. With his role still limited under JJ Redick, the Lakers face growing questions about whether his roster spot is the best use of their available resources. item.title: Savannah teams and runners to watch in GHSA Cross Country state meets
item.description: The GHSA State Cross Country Championships are here as races are set to be run in Carrollton on Friday and Saturday, Nov. 6 and 7. Runners and teams have been under the watchful eye of their coaches as they have been focused on peaking at the right time for the end-of-the-season event. Richmond Hill coach Levi Sybert has his girls and boys teams ready for the Class 7A meet, which will be run on Saturday, after both squads finished second in the Class 7A Sectional teams standings. The boys were led by freshman sensation Liam Penttila, who ran a personal best time of 15:44.22 on the 3.1 mile course to finish second in the race individually. Wildcat senior Eddie Howell was eighth in 16:23.58, one spot ahead of his sophomore teammate Caden Gross who finished in 16:30.29. Junior Derek Feske was 15th in 16:59.91. Junior Chloe Miller led the Wildcat girls with a third place finish in 18:50.02, with senior Gabriella Francis fifth in 19:30.21. Senior Julia Anastasio was 11th in 19:47.30, one place ahead of freshman Lucy Puskar (20:08.71). "Liam (Penttila) is just a freshman but he has a lot of ability and has found his stride this year," Sybert said. "He's a quiet and hard working runner. He stayed in the back of the pack earlier in the year, but now he likes to get out and run with the top dogs. He's a very methodical runner. "Julia (Anastasio) is coming back from a hip injury that slowed her down as a junior and is having a big season," he said "And Chloe has emerged as our No. 1 lately, and with Gabby Francis we have a solid group at the top of our lineup." The Wildcat boys have a chance to win it all, as they did in 2021, Sybert said, and he's hoping for a podium (Top 4) finish for both squads. The Savannah Arts girls are on a quest to win their third straight state crown and took another step toward that goal by winning the Class 2A Sectional 1 meet. The Panthers were led by senior Francie Tedder, who finished second in 19:22.00. Morgan Irvine was third with a time of 20:13.60 and McKay Bennett finished fifth in 20:33.00. Madeline Balthrop was seventh in 20:52.00 and Avae Treece finished 10th in 21:34.70. The Panthers boys squad had a strong team run to finish third in the meet led by Logan Brodhead, who was fourth in 17:30.10 and Nico Klaras, who took eighth with a time of 17:37.10. The Islands girls team won the Class 3A Sectional 1 team title with three girls finishing in the Top 10. Leila Kellison was second in 20:55.90, with Zeycan Agbas sixth in 22:38.60, one spot ahead of Kaileigh Toler (22:39.00). item.title: Missouri basketball vs SLU scout report, score prediction
item.description: For the first time in a quarter-century, Mizzou and SLU men’s basketball teams are meeting on the court. Missouri basketball, fresh off slamming Cleveland State by 61 points in its season-opener, is rolling right into the meat of its beefed-up nonconference slate, traveling for a game Friday, Nov. 6, against in-state rival Saint Louis on a neutral floor at the Enterprise Center in St. Louis. The game tips off at 6 p.m. and airs on ESPNU.The Tigers (1-0) made light work of head coach Dennis Gates’ former team in their season debut, but the warm-up period was short this year. Saint Louis (1-0), which is coached by Josh Schertz, thumped Georgia in the first round of the NCAA Tournament last season before falling to eventual national champion Michigan. Several key members from that Big Dance squad are back for more with the Billikens this year. More: Guard CJ Gunn ruled ineligible, will not play for Missouri basketball this year SLU and Mizzou have not played since December 2001. That hiatus ends Friday evening. Here’s what you need to know about SLU before Friday’s game at Enterprise Center: Will Robbie Avila be available to play for SLU? Mizzou isn’t the only team in the state with some significant November court drama. Standout forward Robbie Avila had a hearing Wednesday for a preliminary injunction against the NCAA. He needs the court order to be able to play for the Billikens this season. Avila was the leading scorer on the SLU team that won 29 games, won the Atlantic-10 regular season title and went to the second round of the NCAA Tournament last season. The 6-foot-10 forward averaged 12.8 points and 4.1 assists per game and shot 41.0% from 3-point range. He’s a difference-maker. The judge indicated that a ruling should come soon. Saint Louis head coach Josh Schertz said that if the result is favorable for Avila, he will play the forward against Missouri . Change on this front could come at any time, so keep your eyes peeled. And Kellen Thames is going to be a real challenge for Mizzou to defend. The high-motor fifth-year guard, listed at 6-6, shot 6-of-6 from the field in SLU’s season-opening win over Lehigh for 15 points and added six rebounds. He’s excellent at getting out in transition and attacking downhill. The Billikens scored 50 points in the paint against Lehigh. They’re going to give Mizzou a test on the interior, and Thames is going to be leading that effort. His father played 128 games for Mizzou between 1993-98 under Norm Stewart and averaged 17.6 points and 8.2 rebounds in his career. He is eighth on MU’s all-time career-points list with 1,689. item.title: Zeeland West vs Battle Creek Central playoff scouting report and prediction
item.description: The second week of the playoffs is here and the Holland area has just one high school team that advanced to the district finals. Here is a look at the matchup in the MHSAA playoffs. More: Zeeland West football rolls past Niles without star running back to advance Battle Creek Central at Zeeland West WHEN: 7 p.m. Friday, Nov. 6 WHERE: Zeeland Stadium RECORDS: Zeeland West 8-2, Battle Creek Central 6-4 PLAYOFF APPERANCES: Zeeland West 22, Battle Creek Central 14 LAST WEEK: Zeeland West beat Niles 60-27, Battle Creek Central beat Battle Creek Harper Creek 41-38 LAST MEETING: First meeting SERIES HISTORY: First meeting SCOUTING REPORT ON BCC: Battle Creek Central only played eight games in the regular season, yet averaged 41 points per game. That was a school record for points per game, passing the 2001 undefeated BCC team which scored 38.5 points per game in the regular season. … Despite missing some time due to injury, junior quarterback Lee Campbell Jr. has nearly 1,000 yards passing and 1,000 yards rushing in basically six outings. In the regular season, Campbell had 922 yards passing and seven touchdown passes. He also has 995 yards rushing and 19 touchdowns. Junior running back Mubarrack Jubril has 1,096 yards rushing and 17 touchdowns. BCC's top receiver, Sir Paris, had 409 yards receiving and three more touchdowns. … In Week 3, BCC and Mattawan scored the most combined points ever in the state of Michigan in 11-player football. Mattawan beat BCC 77-76 in five overtimes. SCOUTING REPORT ON ZW: Running back Brandon Holman missed the first round of the playoffs with an ankle injury. He is expected back this week and will be a key part of the offense. … The Dux run a Wing-T and Power-T offense with double tight ends and three running backs. The offense is an option style and in most plays is decided by how the defense plays it. They have become a state power by finessing this process so defenses and often fans don't know who actually has the ball. … Quarterback Drew Albrecht is the signal caller and is essentially a fourth running back, making it very difficult to plan for four points of attack. He can also throw and it is almost always out of the same formation, so it either will go to a tight end or someone out of the backfield. … The Dux always go for two after a touchdown. Always. The last time they attempted an extra point or a field goal was more than a decade ago. Statistically if the achieve it 50% of the time, they are breaking even, but they average higher than that, giving them an advantage. PREDICTION: Zeeland West 28, Battle Creek Central 14. item.title: The real Hope-Calvin football rivalry begins this week in undefeated clash
item.description: The introduction to the Hope-Calvin football rivalry has come and gone. This year, the real rivalry begins. The first two years, Calvin didn't have a home stadium and had the expected growing pains that any new program would face. Hope was also the dominant force in the MIAA which has led to a couple of pretty lopsided victories for the Flying Dutch. The rivalry will be different this year. Both teams enter the showdown 7-0, tied for first place in the MIAA after the Knights beat Trine 51-20 on Halloween and Hope similarly crushed Kalamazoo. The win over 6-1 Trine proved that Calvin is for real this year, not just beating mediocre teams. Now the Knights will host Hope for the first time in their very own stadium at 1 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 7. Calvin passing attack It has been all about passing for the Knights, who put up 400 yards through the air to quiet the Thunder. They rushed for just 89 yards on 32 carries, but were able to pass at will. Thomas Vaccaro was 23-for-34 passing with four touchdowns. Hunter Hogan and Luke Michmerhuizen each had more than 100 yards receiving. That is a lot to defend. But Hope's secondary has been strong this year, too, and this could be the battle for the game. If Hope can even slow down Calvin's passing attack it would be a huge lift and possible key to victory. Hope defensive line rules One of the big components to The Rivalry so far has been Hope's dominance of the line of scrimmage. While the Knights will be better than in years past on the line, Hope has one of the top D-lines in the country, which could make a huge difference. If Hope can rush Vaccaro and force him to make quick decisions under duress, Tate Bezeau and company will be in the backfield a lot. Hope's run game Hope continues to rush for more than 300 yards a game and slowly put its opponents to sleep. Long drives have produced a lot of short rushing touchdowns this season and that is a sign of control. Hope knows it can control the ball with long, methodical drives. The running backs don't get tired either, because Hope rotates so many in, that there are always fresh legs on the field. If hope can control the ball and limit the passing, the Flying Dutch could clinch a share of the MIAA title. Contact sports editor Dan D’Addona at Dan.D’Addona@hollandsentinel.com. In the post-match press conference, Iraola was pretty blunt about the way the game went, and refused to blame rotation as a possible reason for the lapses in concentration. Select quotes from the presser: “The main reason I can find to lose the game is we conceded [from] three set-pieces. It’s something that we were doing very well in the league, I think we were dealing [with it] quite well until today. We knew it was one of the strengths of Fenerbahce, but we concede from a free-kick, from a corner, even from the long throw at the end.” “They are goals that have hurt us because we have twice gone in front after having good moments, controlling the game, arriving. We found the goals. But after, we conceded in situations that we definitely should defend better.” On his team giving away ‘cheap’ goals… “Yes, as you say, they are cheap goals. They are messy goals. item.title: Time is right for Conlan-backed Hale to flip the page
item.description: Hale's last bout as an amateur was defeat by Patris Mughalzai at the Commonwealth Games [Getty Images] Leaving amateur boxing behind to pursue a professional career was not a tough decision for Belfast's John Paul Hale. An Irish Elite champion in 2021, Hale also collected six Ulster titles and competed at the 2022 and 2026 Commonwealth Games, so the 25-year-old felt "I did as much as I could in the amateur game and now is the right time". Of course, signing off with a medal from this summer's Commonwealth Games in Glasgow would have been ideal, but it wasn't to be as Hale exited the ring frustrated after his opening round defeat by England's Patris Mughalzai in a bout he was docked two points to his opponent's one. Boxing, whichever the code, remains a subjective sport when it comes to officiating, and Hale was more than irked after that loss, his one-finger salute to the officials telling its own story - the same finger that his new manager Michael Conlan flipped in Rio in 2016 when dealing with his own disappointment. "It's a weird one as it's the first time I wasn't upset at myself," Hale told BBC Sport NI when reflecting on that July day. "I knew how hard I had worked before it and had beaten that lad [Mughalzai] before. That time, the referee was letting me work instead of calling 'break' and if he was holding, there were warnings. "I went into that [Commonwealth Games bout] with a mindset that it would be a similar outcome but just felt the referee took it away from me. "It was upsetting because deep down, I knew it was my last opportunity to accomplish what I set out to do [as an amateur]." Same old issues persist in the amateur code While Conlan's reverse to Vladimir Nikitin at the 2016 Olympics would cause outrage and set the wheels in motion for the downfall of amateur boxing's-then ruling body, AIBA [since rebranded to IBA]. World Boxing's approval by the International Olympic Committee has resulted in an exodus to the new body who oversaw the Commonwealth Game but while administration has changed, Hale feels some of the old problems remain. "I don't feel it has changed even though there has been the transition to World Boxing," he opined. "It seemed they [judges] were looking for more aggressive fighters and that suited me, but it didn't feel that way and it just feels like nothing has changed. "When you get to the elite-level fighters, you have different styles they need to sort out how they want people to fight to win. Some can win on the back foot and are not getting the decisions, then others go forward and aren't getting it. "Look at Jude Gallagher at the Commonwealth Games . Loads of others were sickened by it too, a few Scottish fighters were on the end of bad ones [decisions]." item.title: New Bayern deal makes Kane Europe's best-paid player
item.description: New Bayern deal makes Kane Europe's best-paid player After several rounds of negotiations, Bayern Munich finally announced on Thursday that Harry Kane had signed a new contract running until 2029. According to Sky Germany and AZ, Kane will earn a club-record salary, surpassing his previous €25 million per year. The new deal is the most lucrative in Bayern's history, with sources telling The Athletic's David Ornstein that the 33-year-old is now the highest-paid player in European football in terms of guaranteed salary, although some players are thought to be able to earn more overall when bonuses are included. Ornstein also reports that, despite Kane now being 33, Bayern don't see this as his final contract with the club. According to AZ, Bayern CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen held eight rounds of negotiations with the striker's father and brother before finally getting the deal over the line. Kane and his representatives reportedly wanted a contract until 2030, or at least an option to extend the deal until then. However, according to AZ, the final agreement doesn't include such an option. In return, Bayern made concessions to the striker in other areas, including his salary and image rights.

item.description: Motorsport photo The 1980 World Drivers’ Champion, Australia’s Alan Jones, died on the Gold Coast on Thursday. In a statement released on behalf of Jones's family, his wife, Amanda Butler-Davis, said he died following a short illness. He was 80. “We are extremely saddened to announce the passing of our beloved Alan, who passed away on 5 November following a short illness,” Butler-Davis said. “He will be dearly missed and fondly remembered by those closest to him, as well as the many fans whose support he was always grateful for. “Alan dedicated his life to motorsport, building a legacy that will live on through the countless people he touched along the way. “Through his achievements, passion and unmistakable character, both on and off the track, Alan left an enduring mark on the sport both nationally and across the globe. “As a family, we would like to take this opportunity to thank everyone who was part of Alan's journey for the many years of friendship, love and support. He was incredibly fortunate to have so many wonderful people around him.” Jones was born in Melbourne in 1946, the son of businessman and racer Stan Jones, and watched from the sidelines when his father won the 1959 Australian Grand Prix at Longford. The younger Jones repeated the feat at Calder Park in 1980 and remains the last Australian driver to have won the race, which is considered the second-oldest Grand Prix in the world. Jones dabbled in racing in the UK in the 1960s before returning to Australia, before he moved to London in 1970. It took three years for him to establish himself, winning his first Formula 3 race at Silverstone in 1973, the same year he took second in the British F3 championship in a GRD. That team also was to close and Jones’s career looked to have stalled – until Shadow called, having lost lead driver Tom Pryce in a tragic crash in South Africa. In a fairytale result, Jones won in Austria, after a brilliant drive on a wet track, passing local hero Niki Lauda on the way to the first win for an Australian since the retirement of Sir Jack Brabham. Ferrari sounded Jones out for 1978 and Jones thought he had a deal – until Enzo Ferrari reneged, and signed Gilles Villeneuve. Jones was left with an offer from the lowly Williams team, for which owners Frank Williams and Patrick Head had big plans. Jones nearly took the Williams FW06 to the win at Long Beach, but for a broken wing, then again at Brands Hatch, where a gearbox broke. In the US Grand Prix, he was second to Carlos Reutemann’s Ferrari while a new car, the FW07, was being finished back at Grove. item.title: Rafael Benitez confirms he could return to the Premier League
item.description: Rafael Benitez confirms he could return to the Premier League Rafa Benitez Premier League Return Hinges on Finding the Right Project Rafa Benitez wants back in. That is the story, and it is not difficult to understand why. English football still suits him, the Premier League still attracts him, and the rhythm of the competition clearly still grabs him. Speaking on talkSPORT Drive, Benitez made it clear that his current UEFA role has not dulled his appetite for the dugout. If anything, it has sharpened it. He is studying elite matches across Europe, tracking tactical patterns, measuring intensity levels and keeping up with players and styles. That is not the routine of someone winding down. That is someone staying ready. His words were direct: “You know that I’m working now for UEFA, but I’m watching games all the time, and especially the Premier League, because I want to know the players, I want to know their style. “I could see the other day when I was watching Juventus vs Napoli, then I was watching Liverpool vs Arsenal, and you can see the difference. “So I like the Premier League because of the intensity. “Every game, every ball is a challenge. I think it’s fantastic. The problem is that you need to find the right project. Talking about projects in football now is quite complicated.” Premier League Appeal Remains Strong That is the crucial part. Benitez is available, interested and experienced, but he is not walking into any chaos for the sake of a comeback. He has been around too long for that. He knows the difference between a job and a structure. He also knows that too many clubs talk about long-term planning while operating week to week. When asked directly whether that project could be in the Premier League, his answer was brief and clear: “Yeah, yeah, I would be happy with that, for sure.” There is no mystery here. Benitez values control, clarity and a club that understands what it is building. That narrows the field quickly. The Premier League offers money, profile and intensity, but it also offers impatience and noise. Managers get judged fast, often without context. That does not mean Benitez is heading to one of those clubs. It means the market may move soon, and when it does, his name will be part of the conversation. item.title: AEK Athens manager praises Jose Mourinho after 2-3 loss to Real Madrid: ‘I have great admiration for him’
item.description: AEK Athens manager praises Jose Mourinho after 2-3 loss to Real Madrid: ‘I have great admiration for him’ AEK Athens manager Marko Nikolic praised Jose Mourinho following his side’s 3-2 Champions League defeat to Real Madrid . Despite the disappointment of Federico Valverde’s stoppage-time winner, Nikolic expressed his admiration for the Real Madrid manager and insisted his players had every reason to be proud of their performance. Speaking at his post-match press conference (h/t Mundo Deportivo ), the AEK Athens coach analysed the game, explaining that his team had entered the contest with the intention of beating Madrid. Nikolic explains his admiration for Mourinho During his comments, Mourinho’s managerial achievements earned particular recognition from Nikolic, who highlighted his success across multiple leagues and footballing cultures. “I have great admiration for Mourinho. Wherever he goes, he gets results, and he has done so in many countries. “He wins titles in all of them – not just one, but many. To receive a compliment from him is a great honour,” he began saying. Nikolic defends attacking approach against Real Madrid Marko Nikolic’s side gave Real Madrid a run for their money. (Photo by Milos Bicanski/Getty Images) Nikolic was equally keen to emphasise that AEK had approached the match with genuine attacking ambition. His players competed with Real Madrid throughout the encounter, but a missed opportunity during a four-on-two situation proved costly before Valverde settled the contest with a spectacular late strike. “Our approach from the start was to try to win. We didn’t take to the pitch just to manage the game or to make a good impression. “If we’d been fresher, we’d have got a different result. We squandered a four-on-two situation that could have turned the match around. “They stole the ball from us, produced an incredible strike and won,” he explained. Nikolic urges AEK Athens to build on Madrid performance Despite losing, Nikolic refused to allow the result to overshadow his players’ efforts. AEK Athens manager Marko Nikolic is content with his team’s performance. (Photo by Milos Bicanski/Getty Images) He praised their commitment and identified their competitive spirit as an important part of the club’s identity. “We should be proud of our performance. The lads gave it their all. When you see the team giving their all on the pitch, it’s wonderful. “That’s our hallmark and what our fans love about us. It’s impossible to perform at the same level every three days,” he said. Ultimately, he concluded by giving the strongest message possible, stating, “I’m very proud of our team. It’s a shame about the result, but we’re fighters and we’re competitive. “We have no intention of feeling sorry for ourselves. It’s an opportunity to build something better. We’ve still got a long way to go,” he concluded.

item.title: Harry Kane signs record-breaking Bayern Munich contract to become Europe's highest-paid player
item.description: Harry Kane signs record-breaking Bayern Munich contract to become Europe's highest-paid player Harry Kane has signed a record-breaking new contract with Bayern Munich that runs until June 2029 and is believed to make him the highest-paid player in Europe by salary. David Ornstein of The Athletic reported that the three-year extension is the most lucrative deal in Bayern's history, though some players in Europe will still earn more than Kane once bonuses are counted. The 33-year-old's previous terms were due to expire next summer. Both the player and the club were keen to extend the partnership, and Bayern do not see this as his final contract. The Bundesliga champions want to keep the England captain for the foreseeable future. “I feel right at home at FC Bayern. I love the club, the fans and the city of Munich," Kane said in a club statement. "We have a fantastic team and, in Vincent Kompany, a fantastic manager. It makes me very proud to be part of this club. My whole family is very happy here. I was keen to stay. I’m now looking forward to the future and I want to win many more titles with this great club.” A remarkable few weeks for Kane The new deal caps a memorable spell for the striker. Kane won the Ballon d'Or in late October, becoming the first English player to claim the award since 2001, and he is set to become England's most-capped player during the November international break. He has scored 156 goals in 161 games since arriving from Tottenham Hotspur three years ago. In that time he has won two Bundesliga titles, the DFB-Pokal and two Supercups, while the Champions League remains his outstanding target in Munich. The commitment to Germany also means one Premier League ambition looks increasingly out of reach. Alan Shearer's all-time scoring record is now likely to elude Kane, who has opted to remain in the Bundesliga over a potential return to England.

item.title: Career-best Wembanyama display seals Spurs win
item.description: Victor Wembanyama was the NBA's defensive player of the year last season [Getty Images] Victor Wembanyama sank the winning free throw to finish with a career-high 52 points as the San Antonio Spurs beat the Dallas Mavericks 112-111 on Wednesday. The French star, whose previous best was 50 points in 2024, dominated at both ends of the court to also claim 24 rebounds and eight blocks. The 22-year-old is the first player in 52 years with at least 50 points, 20 rebounds and five blocks in a game. He also became the fifth player since 1982 to register at least 50 points and 20 rebounds as San Antonio improved their record to 6-2. Wembanyama reached half-time with 29 points, 15 rebounds, five blocks and two steals, before the Spurs held off a second-half rally by Dallas, who were led by 29 points from Kyrie Irving. "I haven't been feeling great lately," said Wembanyama. "I've been sick for a while. "Today I felt like I got my legs back, so it should be more like this more often." James plays down Finals talk Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid led the Philadelphia 76ers to a 112-106 win over the Detroit Pistons in their top-of-the-table Eastern Conference clash. Brown (30 points) and Embiid (26) led a balanced offensive performance as Philadelphia saw all five starters reach double figures, with LeBron James claiming a double-double of 13 points and 10 rebounds. The 76ers now have the NBA's best record at 8-1 after bringing in Brown and James in the off-season. "It's too early to be talking about the Finals and things of that nature," said James. "We'll just continue to buy into what we want to do. We got a good team." The Los Angeles Lakers beat the Sacramento Kings 116-103 with Luka Doncic scoring a game-high 40 points to reach 308 for the season. The Slovenian star became the first player to pass 300 in his first eight games of a season since Michael Jordan (303) in 1988-89. Doncic was also involved in an incident which led to a fan being removed after throwing the ball at an official, which struck her as she was signalling a Lakers possession. item.title: Honda names Jake Dixon as Joan Mir's substitute for Qatar GP
item.description: Motorsport photo Honda HRC has announced that Joan Mir will be absent this weekend's Qatar Grand Prix after his comeback at Sepang was cut short due to another episode of dizziness and partial loss of vision. British rider Jake Dixon will replace the Spaniard at Losail, returning to the premier class for the first time since he competed two grands prix in 2021 as a substitute for Franco Morbidelli at Petronas SRT. He was classified 19th at Silverstone but was unable to finish the Aragon race. "Joan Mir continues his recovery process after retiring from Sunday's race in Malaysia," Honda explained in its statement. Dixon was part of the world championship paddock between 2019 and 2025, scoring seven victories and 22 podiums in Moto2. This season, the Briton moved up to Honda's factory team in the World Superbike Championship, but his season was marred by injuries. His physical recovery in the second half of the year allowed him to finish inside the top 10 on five occasions. "First of all, I want to thank Honda HRC for this opportunity," Dixon said. "Receiving the call to ride one of these bikes is something fantastic and I'm really looking forward to getting started; I think that, as children, all riders dream of competing for the official Honda MotoGP team. "It's been a while since I last rode a MotoGP bike, so we need to take the weekend calmly and go step by step. I want to wish Joan all the best and I hope to see him back on the bike very soon. It hasn't been an easy year for me either, so I can really relate to his situation. We are going to make the most of this weekend." Dixon will join Luca Marini in Honda's official factory team line-up in Qatar, after the Italian rider recovered in time to be able to travel. "Our goal for this weekend is to build on the performance we showed on Sunday at Sepang. I've been able to spend a few days at home and continue recovering, so my physical condition has improved," said the Italian. "It's a circuit that hasn't always allowed us to make the most of our strengths, but with only three races left to finish the season with Honda, this is the time to go all out and give our best in each of them. I want to wish Joan all the best; having him in the garage is always a boost for both me and the team." Dixon could finish the season in Portimao and Valencia if Mir is unable to recover. The 2020 world champion missed four races between Austria and Australia due to health issues, before returning to action in Malaysia last weekend. While he completed much of the weekend without issues after being declared fit, he was forced to retire early from the grand prix on Sunday as the same health issues resurfaced. item.title: Jason Whitlock accuses LeBron James of influencing Bryce’s role after Arizona debut
item.description: Photo by Harry How/Getty Images Jason Whitlock has questioned Bryce James’ place in Arizona’s basketball team after LeBron James’ youngest son made his first start for the Wildcats. The veteran analyst believes LeBron’s influence, rather than Bryce’s performances, may have played a part in him receiving an opportunity with the college programme. Bryce featured for just six minutes in Arizona’s 84-75 upset defeat to UCLA, recording no points or rebounds and finishing with one assist. Jason Whitlock questions Bryce James’ role with Arizona Whitlock was particularly critical of the limited role Bryce was given during the game and suggested his involvement was more about keeping his father happy than his ability on the court. Speaking in an Instagram video, Whitlock said: “Bryce James is a make-a-swish kid. Arizona, the number 5 team country last night, gave Bryce James, LeBron’s youngest son, three minutes at the beginning of the first half and three minutes at the beginning of the second half, and that’s it.” He then made his criticism of LeBron’s influence even clearer: “He’s a make-a-swish kid, has no business on the Arizona basketball team, and LeBron is forcing them to give him token starts.” Bryce went 0-for-3 from the field and missed both of his three-point attempts against UCLA. However, it was only his first appearance and does not necessarily reflect what he can offer Arizona over the course of the season. The youngster redshirted his freshman year to preserve his eligibility while developing his game and adjusting to college basketball. His brother Bronny also faced scrutiny during his only season at USC, where he averaged 4.8 points, 2.8 rebounds and 2.1 assists. Whitlock has previously questioned LeBron’s decisions regarding Bronny’s basketball career. He suggested the Lakers star could have encouraged his eldest son to pursue American football instead. “Bronny James, with a different father, would be an outside linebacker or free safety on a major college football team, seen as a first- or second-round draft pick,” he said. Bryce now has time to respond to the criticism and establish himself at Arizona. His performances in the coming games will be important as he looks to build his own reputation rather than simply being viewed as LeBron James’ son. item.description: The biggest wins in Champions League history: Como join Liverpool and Real Madrid Como have written their name into the Champions League record books after producing a remarkable 9-1 demolition of Lens. Cesc Fabregas' side became just the third team in the competition's history to win a match by an eight-goal margin, equalling the record set by Liverpool and Real Madrid . Their extraordinary result in France places them alongside two of European football's most famous clubs, and brings back memories of some of the competition's most one-sided encounters. Here, we look back at the biggest winning margins in Champions League history. Liverpool 8-0 Beşiktaş, 06/11/2007 Liverpool became the first team in Champions League era to win by an eight-goal margin after battering Besiktas during the 2007/08 campaign. Runners-up the previous season, Rafael Benitez's side had earned only one point from their first three games before a stunning win over the Turkish side turned their campaign around. Yossi Benayoun scored a hat-trick for the home side, with Peter Crouch and Ryan Babel bagging braces. Steven Gerrard was also on target in a record-setting win for the Reds. Real Madrid 8-0 Malmö, 08/12/2015 Real Madrid matched Liverpool's record scoreline eight years later, with Cristiano Ronaldo predictably at the heart of it. Ronaldo scored four goals as the Swedish side were thrashed at the Bernabeu. Karim Benzema also scored a hat-trick, as the pair became the first two teammates to score trebles in the same Champions League game. Mateo Kovacic completed the rout, for a Real Madrid side that went on to conquer Europe, beating Atletico Madrid in the final. Lens 1-9 Como, 04/11/2026 Como's first-ever Champions League campaign is turning into a memorable one. The Italians trounced Manchester United in a statement result earlier in the league phase, before a record-equalling performance at Lens. Cesc Fabregas' side recorded the biggest-ever away win in the Champions League era, and became only the second team to score nine goals, after Bayern Munich beat Dinamo Zagreb 9-2 in 2024.
